record_identity.title: Trajectory-level boundary erosion under persistent adaptive influence

summary: A governed system maintains a safety, authority, consent, policy or execution boundary at one or more points in an interaction, but fails to preserve that boundary across the cumulative interaction trajectory. Persistent or adaptive influence can therefore use reframing, incremental escalation, repeated probing, contextual accumulation or other course-of-conduct strategies to obtain an outcome that the system previously and correctly rejected, even though the underlying restricted objective, authority state or risk condition has not materially changed.
why_it_matters_to_CAM: Local-turn safety is not equivalent to trajectory-stable safety. A system may correctly refuse an underlying restricted objective when presented directly yet become progressively more permissive when the same objective is distributed across an adaptive multi-turn interaction. Governance therefore needs a course-of-conduct view that preserves materially unchanged safety and authority boundaries across accumulated context rather than treating each turn as an isolated decision.

source_records.source_title: Large reasoning models are autonomous jailbreak agents
source_records.system_or_product: Large reasoning models used as autonomous adversarial agents against target language models
source_records.model_or_algorithm: DeepSeek-R1, Gemini 2.5 Flash, Grok 3 Mini and Qwen3 235B as adversarial LRMs; nine target models including GPT-4o, Claude 4 Sonnet, Gemini 2.5 Flash, Grok 3 and others
source_records.deployment_context: Controlled multi-turn adversarial evaluation in which an LRM receives a system-prompt jailbreak objective and then autonomously plans and conducts a conversation against a target model without further human supervision.
source_records.source_context: Hagendorff, Derner and Oliver report that adversarial LRMs could autonomously plan and conduct persuasive multi-turn attacks against nine target models. The target models ingest the complete conversation history. Direct administration of the harmful benchmark items to target models produced very low harm on average, whereas the adaptive conversational method yielded an overall jailbreak success rate of 97.14% across model combinations. The paper reports gradual escalation, educational and hypothetical reframing, rapport-building, detailed follow-up and other persuasive strategies, with harm scores increasing across interaction trajectories for susceptible targets.
source_records.relevance_note: Primary peer-reviewed experimental evidence that an underlying harmful objective which is usually rejected when presented directly can become actionable after adaptive multi-turn context accumulation, supporting a trajectory-stability failure rather than merely a one-shot prompt-injection mechanism.

primary_artefact_access.access_method: direct public review of the Nature Communications article
limitations: The study is a controlled adversarial evaluation and does not establish real-world malicious deployment prevalence.
The paper demonstrates behavioural safety-boundary erosion but does not expose target-model internal classifier states or prove a specific internal optimisation process.

The attacking LRMs were explicitly authorised by the researchers to conduct jailbreaks; successful attacker conduct is treated as threat/capability evidence rather than as an attacker-side governance failure.

source_records.interpretive_reliance: Relied on for the demonstrated contrast between low-harm direct requests and high-success adaptive multi-turn attacks, the full-history target context, gradual escalation, persuasive adaptation and autonomous attack execution. VIGIL separately abstracts the receiving-system failure as loss of trajectory-level boundary invariance under materially unchanged underlying risk or authority conditions.

evidenced_systems.source_title: Large reasoning models are autonomous jailbreak agents

evidence_projection.inference_boundary: Provider and model identities are taken from the published study. The record does not infer undisclosed target-model internal safety architecture or private deployment behaviour beyond the reported evaluation.

contextual_relations.rationale: FM-0058 governs the influencing actor's instrumental manipulation or coercive influence over another decision-maker. FM-0071 governs the receiving system's failure to maintain a materially unchanged safety or authority boundary across cumulative adaptive pressure. The repair locus differs: constrain the influencing actor for FM-0058; preserve trajectory-level boundary invariance for FM-0071.

FM-0009 concerns non-revocable conversational context contamination. FM-0071 does not require poisoned or non-revocable state; ordinary valid conversation history can become the medium through which an unchanged restricted objective is gradually reframed until enforcement changes.

FM-0022 requires lower-authority or untrusted content to be elevated into instruction or execution authority. FM-0071 requires instability of a previously operative boundary across an adaptive interaction trajectory and does not require any source-authority elevation.

FM-0047 concerns policy laundering when a broader system delegates to a specialised adversarial agent and imports its expanded conduct into an otherwise legitimate task. The Nature experiment deliberately authorises the attacker to jailbreak; FM-0071 instead captures the target-side loss of boundary invariance.

FM-0067 requires attacker-controlled state to persist beyond the originating content or interaction and later reactivate. FM-0071 occurs within an ongoing trajectory and requires progressive boundary erosion, not cross-session hostile-state persistence.

failure_mode_definition: A failure mode in which a governed system initially and correctly maintains a safety, authority, consent, policy or execution boundary against an underlying restricted objective, but fails to preserve that boundary across the cumulative interaction trajectory. The counterparty may adapt to refusals through reframing, incremental escalation, repeated probing, contextual layering, persuasion, decomposition or other course-of-conduct strategies. The failure occurs when the system becomes materially more permissive even though the underlying restricted objective, authority state, policy basis or risk condition has not legitimately changed. The relevant governed object is therefore the trajectory as well as the individual turn.
failure_threshold: The threshold requires: (1) an underlying restricted objective, authority boundary or risk condition that remains materially stable across the interaction; (2) one or more earlier points at which the system maintains or expresses the relevant boundary, or controlled evidence that direct presentation of the objective is rejected or materially less permissive; (3) persistent or adaptive interaction that changes framing, sequencing, context or pressure in response to prior system behaviour; and (4) later weakening, bypass or extinguishment of the boundary without a legitimate change in authority, policy, factual condition or risk classification. Ordinary persuasion where reconsideration is authorised, genuine factual change, explicit authorised override, benign iterative refinement, one-shot jailbreaks, and mere repeated attack attempts that never alter the boundary are excluded.

failure_classification.severity_assessment_basis: S1 reflects peer-reviewed experimental evidence that adaptive multi-turn interaction can convert harmful objectives that are largely rejected when presented directly into successful jailbreak trajectories across multiple widely used models, including high-harm outputs in sensitive domains. The study is controlled research rather than confirmed malicious deployment, so realised real-world harm and prevalence remain bounded.
failure_classification.severity_assessment_gap: Real-world malicious exploitation prevalence, deployment-specific downstream consequences and internal target-model control architecture are not established by the study.
failure_classification.likelihood: demonstrated across multiple model combinations in controlled evaluation; deployment likelihood depends on access to sustained interaction and model-specific resistance
failure_classification.confidence: high for the behavioural mechanism demonstrated in the study; bounded for generalisation to all models and non-conversational boundary types
failure_classification.failure_scope: stateful conversational and agentic systems repeatedly evaluating safety, authority, consent, policy or execution boundaries
failure_classification.recurrence_pattern: May recur whenever an adversary can observe refusals or boundary signals, adapt its strategy and accumulate context while the receiving system evaluates safety primarily at the local-turn level.
failure_classification.persistence: Persists for as long as the system lacks trajectory-level preservation or revalidation of materially unchanged boundaries under adaptive cumulative interaction.
failure_classification.reproducibility: Testable through authorised controlled evaluations comparing direct presentation of a restricted objective against adaptive multi-turn trajectories that preserve the same underlying objective while varying framing, sequencing and accumulated context.
failure_classification.visibility: Potentially low in turn-by-turn review because individual messages may appear benign or only mildly escalatory; the failure becomes apparent when the interaction is analysed as a course of conduct.

mechanism_or_cause: failure to preserve materially unchanged boundary state
faceted_analysis.reporting_notes: Treat the attacker-side autonomous jailbreak capability as a threat/capability signal. This FM is target-side and concerns loss of trajectory-level boundary invariance. The demonstrated propagation is local to the evaluated interaction; possible propagation across agent-to-agent interfaces remains a bounded prospective risk. Repair responsibility may lie across provider, deployer and orchestration governance rather than one component. Do not infer subjective coercion, intent or internal optimisation drift from behavioural evidence alone.
